values_equal called float() on reference outputs; factorial-class ints
(>1e308) raised OverflowError and killed the live repro at case 83/164.

protection: route_one degrades any differential_check exception to an

per-case JSONL as it goes so a crash preserves completed rows.

tasks.body:
MIN_DISAGREEMENTS=2: reject only on >=2 disagreeing consensus inputs. The
127-accept replay's raw gate produced 12 rejects = 3 catches + 9 false
alarms; 6/9 false alarms disagreed on exactly one generated input (incl.
the only quality-losing row, HumanEval/124: local-pass + cloud-fail), while
the catches disagreed on 15/4/2. One disagreement is noise-shaped; two are
systematic — the same >=2-of-K posture as tool_judge's solver consensus.
Threshold chosen post-hoc on this run; live confirmation required before
any headline cites it (stated in findings Era 22 and current_state).

report code-judge: --min-disagree re-derives cached rejects from the stored
mismatch counts, so threshold sweeps are free; fresh checks cache the raw
(threshold-1) verdict.

Final replay (recorded 164-task HumanEval+ run, k=3, min_disagree=2):
fail-recall 22/32 -> 25/32, wrong answers served 10 -> 7, over-escalations
15 -> 19 (all on cloud-pass rows), routed 0.921 -> 0.939 @ $10.04/1k vs
cloud 0.976 @ $35.97 — 96.2% of cloud quality at a 72.1% cost cut.

2 new tests (33 total); fast lane 1542 green. Brain: journal
2026-08-04-code-judge, findings Era 22, current_state refresh.
tasks.subject: feat: code-judge reject threshold + full-replay result; brain Era 22

tasks.body: A model that emitted an opening ```lang fence but was truncated before the closing fence caused extract_code to return the raw output verbatim — leaving a literal '```python' as the first line of 'code' and breaking anything that ran it (coder role uses extract_code in postprocess). Now strips a lone opening fence (and any dangling close). Found while scoring the verifiable-reward bench; rescued 2 qwen3.5 cases (0.765->0.882 pass@1). Adds test_postprocess.py.
tasks.subject: fix(workers): extract_code tolerates unclosed/truncated fences

tasks.body: code's generic keywords (def/return/implement/function) matched almost any prompt that quotes code as context, and the security list checked singular 'vulnerability' not the common plural. Result: 0/80 real security-intent prompts classified as security; code absorbed 62.5% of real traffic. Reorder so intent buckets are checked before code (code last), broaden the stem to 'vulnerab', add 'secret', drop colliding 'check' from review. 14/14 real security prompts now correct; code's share drops to 8.75%. 9 regression tests added. See brain/state/findings.md Era 6.
tasks.subject: fix(routing): bucket classifier misrouted intent traffic to code

tasks.body: For code/test/refactor/debug, model output that doesn't execute (syntax error, bad import, crash) now flips the outcome to failed so reward short-circuits to 0 — the heuristic quality scorer can't see this (findings.md Era 9), and capping quality alone is toothless since success is the bulk of the code-bucket weight. Mirrors the existing strict_verify success-downgrade at the same point in the reward path. Conservative: catches 'doesn't run', not 'wrong' (organic traffic has no gold tests). On by default; MAHORAGA_EXEC_GATE=off disables. Runs model code in a short-timeout subprocess (same posture as tools/code_exec). Verified end-to-end live: valid code passes, prose-in-code-bucket fails. 14 tests.
tasks.subject: feat(routing): live execution gate for code-producing buckets

tasks.body:
OllamaWorker now retries transient cold-load failures (HTTP 5xx while a
model loads, or ReadError/ReadTimeout/RemoteProtocolError when a model is
swapped in on a memory-tight machine) up to 2x with 2s->4s backoff. 4xx
client errors and ConnectError still fail fast so a genuinely-down server
isn't masked by backoff. Safe because the response is fully buffered and no
event is yielded until the stream completes, so a retry rebuilds cleanly.
Hardens live traffic (idle-eviction cold loads) as well as bench runs.

Surfaced by Phase 4 (bench_run_id=19): 6/50 qwen3.5 tasks failed exactly
this way, all clustered at the first task after a model swap.

Also drops the qwen3-14b arm (enabled: false, bandit history preserved):
on the 50-row verifiable bank it landed mid-pack (pass@1 0.880), beaten by
the 5.3 GB granite (0.900) — no correctness edge for ~2x the RAM on a 16 GB
machine. Roster is now granite4.1-8b + qwen3.5.

Includes 5 regression tests for the retry paths and the Phase 4 brain
records (journal, findings Era 11, current_state). Full suite: 1430 passed.
tasks.subject: fix: retry Ollama cold-load transients; drop qwen3-14b arm

tasks.body:
The published cloud arm bills through the `claude` CLI on an interactive
subscription. That is accurate accounting and a bad precondition: "reproducible
by anyone" quietly meant "anyone who pays for Claude". `--cloud-arm claude`
runs the same model over the Anthropic API with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead.

The arm choice is an authentication decision and nothing else. Both workers
frame the prompt through workers.base._build_prompt and name the same model, so
routed pass@1 stays comparable across arms; a test pins the shared framing,
because a divergence there would silently make cross-arm runs incomparable
while still producing plausible numbers. The always-cloud dollar column is NOT
comparable — API and subscription bill differently — and the docs say so
wherever the flag appears.

Reachability failures are now typed (CloudArmUnavailable) and carry the fix in
the message. It matters in two places that cannot show a traceback: the serving
cascade, which degrades to serving the local answer and where this message is
the only trace of why escalation stopped; and `bench repro` preflight, which
must fail in seconds rather than hours in. Preflight also stops looking for a
binary that an API-backed arm does not have.

The cloud arm now survives into the run ledger notes, since it changes what the
always-cloud column means. agents.yaml gains an explicit `worker:` key, with
the kind inferred from the arm id so existing rosters keep working.
tasks.subject: feat: reproduce the benchmark without a Claude subscription

tasks.body:
A launchd job inherits nothing from the shell: no user variables, and a
PATH of /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin. The plist had no
EnvironmentVariables block at all, so running Mahoraga as a daemon meant
every MAHORAGA_* knob was pinned to its code default with no way to set
it, and `claude`/`ollama` were unresolvable — the escalation arm would
degrade to serving local answers without an error anyone would notice.

`install` now bakes in a PATH covering the venv, ~/.local/bin, and
Homebrew, plus any KEY=VALUE lines from ~/.mahoraga-v2/service.env, and
echoes the resulting settings so a misconfigured daemon is visible at
install time.

Two adjacent traps fixed while here, both of which produced a CLI that
reported success while the daemon was not running:

- `launchctl load` prints "Load failed: 5: Input/output error" and still
  exits 0, so the return code cannot be trusted — verify via `list`;
- a label can be marked disabled in launchd's persistent database, which
  survives unload, reinstall, and reboot, and fails every subsequent load
  with that same opaque errno 5 until `launchctl enable` clears it.

14 tests.
tasks.subject: fix: give the launchd daemon a configuration surface

tasks.body:
- reward_learner: replace hard OLS weight swap with EMA blend (α=1/K,
  K=20 by default). Per-step weight shift ≤5% of OLS-shift, keeping the
  drift detector below its alert threshold during weight transitions.
  MAHORAGA_OLS_TRANSITION_STEPS=1 collapses back to hard replacement.
- reward_learner: fix _load() bug — self._learned assignment was outside
  the for-loop body, silently discarding all but the last bucket on load.
- reward_learner: remove nested `import os`; add module-level import.
- app.py: fix set_routing_strategy fallback from "linucb" to "linucb_per_bucket".
- test_per_bucket_default: 3 smoke tests for per-bucket default (Step 3).
- test_ols_drift_interaction: 3 adversarial tests for Fix B (Step 4):
    positive direction (OLS fires, no DriftAlert raised),
    negative direction (genuine collapse, DriftAlert + quarantine fires),
    math invariant (blend step == 1/K of OLS-shift).
- spec: 3 editorial fixes per user review (§9.1 pair #4, §11.1, §15 step 12).
tasks.subject: feat(routing): OLS Fix B smoothed weight transition + Step 3/4 tests

tasks.body:
The delegation funnel's first real reading was 0.0% over 170 delegable actions,
and it was worthless. ~/.claude.json pointed the MCP server at a bare `python`
that does not exist on this machine, so the server never started and `run_task`
was never listed. Four weeks of "you never delegate" was four weeks of a dead
interpreter path — and nothing in the output could tell the difference. The rate
looked exactly like a behavioural finding.

A rate cannot be read without knowing the tool was there. The MCP server now
records one fact when it serves its tool list — the moment `run_task` becomes
visible to the agent — and the funnel reads it back as an interpretation:

  no-delegable-work      nothing shaped like delegable work; there is no ratio
  tool-liveness-unknown  delegable work, but the tool was never observed alive,
                         so a low rate cannot be told apart from a dead tool.
                         This is the state the 2026-09-10 reading was in.
  tool-available-unused  the tool was demonstrably there and nothing was
                         delegated. The only case where 0% means what it looks
                         like.
  measured               a rate with a live tool behind it.

`orch metrics funnel` now refuses to endorse a liveness-unknown rate: it still
prints the number, and prints above it that the number is not readable and why.

Design notes:

- Liveness is its own event, so it touches NEITHER half of the ratio — only
  whether the ratio is readable. Test-pinned: adding 20 liveness rows changes
  no counter and no rate, just the interpretation.
- The row carries an empty session, so editor restarts cannot inflate the
  session count. Also pinned.
- The writer (backend/mcp/funnel_liveness.py) is stdlib-only and
  fire-and-forget, the same tradeoff scripts/claude_code_funnel_hook.py makes:
  it runs on the tool-discovery path, so it must add no meaningful latency,
  import nothing heavy, and never propagate an exception. A liveness probe that
  can break tool discovery is worse than no liveness probe.
- That means the log path and event name live in two files. If they drift,
  liveness rows get written and silently never counted — the original failure
  mode wearing a different hat — so a test pins writer and reader to the same
  values.
- The window filter applies to liveness too: a tool that was alive last month
  says nothing about this month.
- MAHORAGA_FUNNEL_LIVENESS=off disables the write.

13 tests; suite 1743 green.

NOTE ON MERGE ORDER: this branch is based on feat/resource-meter (PR #41), not
main, because it builds on that PR's funnel_report refactor. Merge #41 first, or
retarget this PR's base to main after #41 lands — per the stacked-PR lesson from
the #22/#23 phantom merge, never merge the parent while a child still points at
it.
